Companion Animal Travel Desk: Transfer and Lounge Handling

This section sets the minimum conduct required for safe, calm, and consistent service to companion animals and their travelers. Every action must protect welfare, preserve trust, and keep the handoff orderly.

Staff must move carriers with steady hands, keep routes clear, and speak in a low, reassuring voice. The ground team must inspect latches, labels, and ventilation before any transfer, and must never rush a carrier past a doorway, cart, or service line. If a traveler appears anxious, the agent must give brief, direct guidance and avoid crowded language. Where a pet is checked in for lounge support, the desk must keep records accurate, observe identification carefully, and maintain clean separation between incoming and outgoing cases. <<FACT F002>> The desk must follow the same standard for every animal, whether the case is routine or sensitive, because uneven handling creates delay and distress.

Lounge access requires close attention to entry control, cleanliness, and calm supervision. Staff must confirm the right carrier, confirm the traveler’s handoff instructions, and ensure that food, water, and rest areas are arranged without confusion. <<FACT F019>> No one may leave a companion animal unattended in a public holding space, and no one may improvise a transfer method that has not been approved. If equipment fails, or if a pet shows agitation, breathing difficulty, or escape behavior, staff must stop the process at once and alert the senior coordinator without debate.

Communication must remain concise, kind, and actionable at every stage. Use plain language, avoid speculation, and give only the steps the traveler needs next. Note any irregular condition immediately, because late reporting weakens the whole service chain. When in doubt, pause the transfer, protect the animal, and seek direction from the duty lead.

For urgent guidance, contact the senior coordinator through the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
